title: A video caller declares a digital arrest
mechanism_summary: Impostors accuse someone of involvement in a crime and demand money to settle the supposed case. They may keep the person continuously visible on a video call until demands are met.
suggested_beats: An apparent officer announces a case.
The person is ordered to remain on camera.
End the coercive contact and report through official channels.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone frightened by an apparent police accusation
why_it_works: Authority and isolation reduce opportunities to question the demand.

title: A relative is supposedly in police custody
mechanism_summary: A caller claims that a loved one is detained after a crime or accident. Money is demanded to compromise the supposed case.
suggested_beats: A caller announces trouble involving family.
Release depends on an immediate payment.
Verify the relative's situation independently.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone worried about a loved one
why_it_works: Fear for family can make an unverified official claim persuasive.

title: A tax caller threatens arrest over invented debt
mechanism_summary: A caller impersonates a tax agency and demands immediate payment. Threats of arrest or other consequences pressure the recipient to comply.
suggested_beats: An apparent tax official announces debt.
Payment becomes a condition of avoiding arrest.
Contact the tax agency through a trusted channel.
why_it_works: Fear of punishment can override doubts about an unexpected demand.

title: An identity warning demands a protective transfer
mechanism_summary: An impostor claims a person's identity or accounts are implicated in a serious problem. The person is told to move money to protect it, placing it under the scammer's control.
suggested_beats: An apparent official raises an identity alarm.
Protection requires moving money.
Verify the claim before making any transfer.
why_it_works: A threat is presented alongside a false route to safety.

title: A workplace reference makes a death threat feel immediate
mechanism_summary: A cyberstalker sent anonymous threats that referred to the target's workplace. Those references made the online campaign intrude on the person's sense of physical safety.
suggested_beats: Threatening messages arrive.
The sender refers to the workplace.
Preserve messages and seek police support.
why_it_works: Knowledge of a real location can make an anonymous threat feel close.

title: A network threatens exposure to force compliance
mechanism_summary: An abusive online network threatens to reveal private information or intimate material. The threats are used to coerce escalating harmful behavior.
suggested_beats: An online connection gains private information.
Exposure becomes a condition for obedience.
Seek trusted support and report the coercion.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone pressured by an abusive online group
why_it_works: Fear of exposure can isolate the target from people who could help.

title: A swatting threat creates fear of armed response
mechanism_summary: Abusive online actors threaten false emergency reports against a target. The threat exploits the danger of sending emergency responders to an invented incident.
suggested_beats: An online actor issues a demand.
Refusal brings a swatting threat.
Report the threat to police and seek support.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone targeted by an abusive network
why_it_works: Threatened real-world consequences can make online coercion feel inescapable.

title: A business threatens a reviewer into silence
mechanism_summary: A business uses intimidation or an unfounded legal threat to suppress a negative review. Other consumers then see a distorted picture of customer experience.
suggested_beats: A customer posts a negative review.
A threat demands its removal.
Keep evidence of the threat and report the conduct.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone reviewing a poor purchase experience
why_it_works: Fear of conflict or legal expense can silence legitimate criticism.
